inputSnapshot.learningGoal: TypeScript discriminated union과 runtime validation을 배우고 싶다

round.generationRationale: Generated 8 semantically distinct candidates leveraging discriminated unions and runtime validation across different problem domains: API validation (debugging focus), event routing (decoupling), form states (UI feedback), database results (schema-driven), payment webhooks (business domain), config composition (precedence), plugins (extensibility), and error recovery (resilience). Each emphasizes different aspects of discriminated unions (response types, event routing, state machines, schema variants, provider discrimination, source tracking, hook contracts, error classification) and different target users (backend, frontend, DevOps, tool builders). Candidates 1 and 5 naturally connect to stated interest in API debugging and developer tools, while others explore broader applicability of the learning goal in various domains.

diversityCheck.rationale: Candidates span distinct domains (API validation, event systems, forms, databases, payments, config, plugins, errors), target different users (backend, frontend, DevOps, framework developers), use different interactions (validation routing, event dispatch, state machine, schema introspection, webhook decoding, source merging, plugin loading, recovery dispatch), have different data shapes (responses, messages, field states, rows, events, config objects, hooks, errors), and appeal to different motivations (debuggability, modularity, UX feedback, schema safety, real-world payments, configuration flexibility, extensibility, resilience).

candidates.title: Config File Parser with Environment Overrides
candidates.summary: Build a configuration loader that treats config values as discriminated unions of file-sourced vs. environment vs. default, validating and merging them at runtime.
candidates.coreInteraction: Load config from file, check environment variables, check defaults, merge using union to track provenance, validate merged result.
candidates.usageMoment: When setting up applications that need flexible configuration from multiple sources.
candidates.appeal: Transparent config sourcing; validates all sources consistently; learner sees unions solve composition and precedence.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions track config source and value type; validation ensures merged config is correct.

evaluation.rationale: Config sources naturally form union variants.
Common pattern but not API-focused.
Every application has config; learner can generalize.
Config mismatches cause runtime errors; validation prevents them early.
MVP is file + env + defaults + validation.
File I/O and parsing are minimal.
Reusable module in any application.
Focuses on source tracking and composition.

candidates.title: Error Recovery Logger with Action Paths
candidates.summary: Build a structured error logger where each error is a discriminated union representing its type, and recovery actions are validated and applied based on error variant.
candidates.coreInteraction: Catch error, discriminate type, look up recovery actions, validate action is valid for error type, execute and log.
candidates.usageMoment: When building systems that need to recover automatically from known errors without human intervention.
candidates.appeal: Maps real error types to recovery strategies; learner sees unions encode domain knowledge; improves system resilience.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions represent error types; validation ensures only appropriate recovery actions execute.
risks: Recovery actions may fail or loop
Error context can be lost in translation

evaluation.rationale: Error types are inherently discriminated and recoverable.
Systems design concern; not directly API debugging.
Every production system logs and recovers errors.
Beginner encounters unexpected errors; sees validation prevent bad recovery.
MVP: catch, discriminate, validate, execute without storage.
Async and logging are supported by agents.
Reusable error handling layer.
Focuses on recovery strategy dispatch.

candidates.title: API Request/Response Type Guard
candidates.summary: Build a CLI tool that validates REST API responses against declared schemas using discriminated unions to handle multiple success and error response types.
candidates.coreInteraction: Load API specs, send requests, validate responses against union types that distinguish status codes and error categories.
candidates.usageMoment: During API development and integration testing when responses vary by endpoint.
candidates.appeal: Catches mismatches early and doubles as live documentation of what responses actually look like.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions encode response variants, runtime validation checks actual payloads against declared types.
risks: Response may drift from spec over time

evaluation.rationale: Discriminated unions encode response variants, runtime validation checks actual payloads against declared types.
Aligns with stated interest in developer tools and API debugging.
Developers already use OpenAPI and need validation; easy to plug into workflows.
Beginner can see patterns emerge naturally through real API data.
MVP scope is well-bounded: load spec, validate, report errors.
HTTP and CLI are lightweight; focus stays on type logic.
Standalone CLI tool, no infrastructure needed.
Focuses on response validation rather than request building.

candidates.title: Payment Gateway Webhook Handler
candidates.summary: Build a webhook receiver that decodes and validates payment events from different providers as discriminated union message types.
candidates.coreInteraction: Register webhook endpoint, receive events, discriminate by provider and event type, validate and dispatch to handlers.
candidates.usageMoment: When integrating Stripe, PayPal, or similar payment systems into applications.
candidates.appeal: Real-world scenario; events are inherently variant-rich; learner sees unions solve a concrete business problem.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions represent payment events from different gateways; runtime validation ensures only valid signatures are processed.

evaluation.rationale: Multiple providers and events create natural union scenarios.
Practical but not tied to API debugging stated interest.
Nearly every SaaS needs webhook handling; reusable pattern.
Real events and signatures teach security and validation together.
MVP: receive, verify, parse, route without storing.
HTTP and crypto are standard; focus on type logic.
Middleware or service module.
Emphasizes multi-provider discrimination and security.

candidates.title: Database Query Result Parser
candidates.summary: Build a query builder that generates TypeScript types for database results and validates rows using discriminated unions to represent different table row structures.
candidates.coreInteraction: Connect to database, inspect schema, generate row types as discriminated unions, parse results and validate structure.
candidates.usageMoment: When writing queries and needing certainty that result shapes match expectations.
candidates.appeal: Eliminates manual type declarations; catch schema drift early; makes queries self-documenting.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions represent different row types; runtime validation confirms query results match declared schemas.
risks: Database connection setup varies by provider

evaluation.rationale: Different query shapes naturally map to union variants.
Backend-focused; API debugging interest is tangential.
ORM and query builders already exist; learner extends patterns.
Schema is external truth; validation failures are obvious.
MVP: connect, introspect, generate, validate single result type.
Database setup can be tedious; consider mock data alternative.
Standalone tool or library.
Schema-driven rather than user-input-driven.

candidates.title: Plugin System with Type-Safe Hooks
candidates.summary: Build a plugin loader where each plugin exports hooks as discriminated union types and the system validates and invokes only matching hook handlers.
candidates.coreInteraction: Define hook interface as union, load plugins, discover their hooks, validate hook signatures, call matching handlers.
candidates.usageMoment: When building extensible systems where plugins need to hook into typed lifecycle events.
candidates.appeal: Learner sees how libraries enforce plugin contracts; explores advanced union patterns; practical for tool builders.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions define hook contracts; runtime validation ensures plugins implement correct signatures.

evaluation.rationale: Hook systems naturally use union patterns.
Framework-level concern; not API debugging.
Plugin pattern exists in tools; learner can adapt.
Beginner sees contract violations at load time.
Module loading adds complexity; consider local plugins first.
Module introspection and loading require careful setup.
Extensible framework library.
Focuses on contract validation and discovery.

candidates.title: Form Validator with Multi-Step Errors
candidates.summary: Build a form validation engine that represents field values as discriminated unions of valid/invalid/pending states and collects per-field errors at runtime.
candidates.coreInteraction: Define fields with validators, bind to input changes, collect and display errors as state transitions through union variants.
candidates.usageMoment: When building web forms with real-time feedback and multi-field dependencies.
candidates.appeal: Type-safe form handling; errors are predictable and debuggable; beginner sees unions in familiar UI context.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions model field states; validators run at runtime and narrow to error or success variant.

evaluation.rationale: Forms naturally have multiple field states; unions fit perfectly.
Generic web pattern but doesn't leverage API debugging interest.
Every web project validates forms; learner can reuse immediately.
Beginner sees immediate visual feedback on type correctness.
Can start with synchronous validators and expand.
DOM APIs are simple; focus on validation logic.
Reusable library or framework integration.
Focuses on state machines rather than message routing.

candidates.title: Event Bus with Typed Message Routing
candidates.summary: Build an in-memory event system where publishers emit discriminated union messages and subscribers receive only the events they've declared interest in.
candidates.coreInteraction: Register handlers for specific event types, emit events, router matches and delivers only matching messages.
candidates.usageMoment: When decoupling components that need to react to state changes without direct calls.
candidates.appeal: Clean separation of concerns; easy to add new event types without rewriting handlers.
candidates.technologyNecessity: Discriminated unions ensure type safety across handler registration and delivery; validation confirms payloads match declared types.
risks: Memory usage if events pile up
Circular event emissions hard to debug

evaluation.rationale: Core exercise in routing different union variants by type.
Useful in large apps but not tied to stated API debugging interest.
Event patterns exist in most frameworks; learner can port knowledge.
Beginner naturally encounters type mismatches when registering wrong handlers.
Simple queue and type matching; MVP is tight.
No external dependencies; pure TypeScript.
Library that integrates anywhere.
Emphasizes runtime dispatch and handler registration.
